candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest labels this binary MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking (SHAP +0.0066 to +0.0115). The evidence is a diffuse set of small contributions with no single dominant feature. Most of the n-grams are generic call/stack-frame and register-manipulation sequences that ordinary compiled code also produces: CALL PUSH (freq 0.0354), MOV PUSH (0.0421), PUSH CALL (0.0505), ADD PUSH, SUB PUSH, POP PUSH, MOV LEAVE, CALL RET and POP CALL. The high frequencies of these sequences show a call-heavy, stack-argument-passing code style, but they do not point to mining behavior. A few rare n-grams are more suggestive: CMP SHLD (0.000094), SBB INC (0.000075), SHL NEG (0.000019) and POP XOR (0.000302). SHLD, SBB and shift/negate sequences can appear in multi-precision or bit-manipulation arithmetic, which is loosely compatible with hashing or crypto routines. However, they are also found in ordinary arithmetic and compiler-generated helper code, and at these frequencies they are weak evidence. Rare sequences such as PUSH RET (0.000019), POP LEA (0.000075) and POP OR (0.000132) may reflect unusual control flow or hand-crafted or packed code, but the evidence does not show this. No function-level attribution, API names, strings or loop-density measures are provided, so nothing ties these n-grams to mining routines, stratum-style communication or persistence. The model's confidence is very high and the uniformly positive SHAP direction supports a malicious classification. The n-gram content itself is not specific enough to confirm cryptojacking rather than another malware family or an artifact of compiler or packer style. This justifies a low-confidence tier pending further analysis.
